language-modes.note: Implemented 2026-08-23, replacing an "absent" row. The mechanism is app/renderer/src/text-boundary.ts, mounted as `h` in app/renderer/src/dc-runtime.tsx -- the element factory every compiled template is built from -- so all three modes (en/yue/both) reach the compiled renderer without any generated file being edited. The `lang_mode` control went into the design and recompiled byte-identically; App.tsx intercepts it in setVal, applies it live and persists it through durable storage, restoring it on mount. PARTIAL rather than implemented, and deliberately so: the catalog covers 187 of roughly 217 design labels, so 21 of the 44 canonical features still render English in every mode. See app/locales/feature-registry.json for the per-feature breakdown, which is recomputed from the catalog by tests/contracts/language-modes.test.mjs and cannot be edited into agreement. An untranslated string renders English rather than a placeholder.

funny-levels.note: No funny-level slider or copy-styling mechanism exists. Notification and dialog copy in App.tsx and the compiled console (this.fire/this.toast) is fixed text with no tone variation.

dialog-emojis.note: Implemented 2026-08-23 as app/renderer/src/dialog-emojis.ts: a persisted toggle, off by default, decorating a dialog heading and body and nothing else. buildDialog enforces the boundary by shape rather than by everyone remembering it -- an emoji never reaches a button, an action label or an accessible name, because a screen reader announces an emoji by its Unicode description and a decorated accessible name is heard on every focus. Decoration does not stack on a re-render and an unrecognised stored value reads as off. Control dlg_emoji went into the design and came back through the compiler; App.tsx acts on it in the same setVal interception the language mode uses.

dim-sum-surprise.note: Implemented 2026-08-23 as app/renderer/src/dim-sum-surprise.ts. A one-in-ten draw at startup, non-blocking, focus-preserving and self-dismissing, suppressed entirely during a first run, an error path, an update, a mid-task flow or quiet hours -- those clauses are what make an un-optable surprise polite, so each is enforced here rather than trusted to the caller. Exactly one draw per launch, because a second would make the real rate higher than the stated one, and the probability boundary is exclusive for the same reason. Every dish carries both names and alt text naming it, so it reaches a screen-reader user. Images are bundled local assets, never URLs. Deliberately has no control and no off switch: storedPreferenceIsIgnored() states that as a fact a test can check, and an older profile carrying "off" simply rejoins the draw.

regex-builder.note: A real regex-capable control is wired: App.tsx binds readings.regexMatchLabel() to a live regex-match count (App.tsx line 889, readings.ts lines 356-360), and the compiled console tab-close filter (generated/console.tsx applyTabFilter, near line 4459) evaluates typed text as new RegExp(q, "i") with a plain-text fallback. Neither is the full guided builder (literal/class/anchor/group construction, flags UI, capture-group display) the contract requires; it is a single pattern field with live match feedback.

changelog-viewer.note: Wired and reachable: App rail > App > Changelog renders every version parsed from a real build-time bundle of this repository's own tag history (scripts/bundle-changelog.mjs -> generated/changelog-bundle.ts), with search (plain text + regex toggle), a date range filter, copy and Markdown export, and per-change commit links validated against real commits (tests/ui/changelog-wired.test.tsx). Confirmed rendering real entries in the built Electron app via headless CDP. Remaining gap: the date filter is typed ISO fields plus range presets, not the full month/year-jump calendar grid the contract describes.

external-editor-handoff.note: Implemented 2026-08-23 as app/renderer/src/external-editor.ts with four controls in the design, acted on through App.tsx. Detects installed editors (PATH first, then absolute fallbacks in order), persists the choice, and lets one be added by hand. VS Code is a first-class export rather than a row in a list, because anything exportable has to be openable in it, and opening a folder carries the workspace-root arguments so a file tree appears rather than a bare file. Nothing is launched through a shell: a plan carries an executable and an argument list passed separately and has no joined command line for a target to be interpolated into, so a path with a space stays one argument and a path carrying shell metacharacters is inert. A hand-added editor is validated as a bare executable and refuses operators and quotes. An editor that has been uninstalled is never silently replaced with another. The copy treats an editor as an optional integration rather than a missing prerequisite, since the console is complete without one.

complete-exports.note: app/renderer/src/export.ts (547 lines, tested by tests/ui/export.test.tsx) implements multi-format export logic, but is never imported by App.tsx or any mounted component.

bulk-actions.note: app/renderer/src/bulk.ts (336 lines, tested by tests/ui/bulk.test.tsx) implements bulk selection/action logic, but is never imported by App.tsx or any mounted component. accessibility.note: No dedicated accessibility mechanism (focus management beyond default DOM behavior, ARIA audit, reduced-motion handling) was found in App.tsx or the compiled console source.

responsive-sizing.note: The compiled console carries a per-screen narrow flag (App.tsx line 709, narrow: true) used to pick a narrower layout for at least one screen, but there is no evidence of a systematic responsive strategy (100/125/150/200% scale handling, narrow-width tab collapse) across the app.

personal-vocabulary-upload.note: Corrected 2026-08-23, and the correction is the point: this row previously read "implemented -- fully wired into App.tsx", which was true of load, clear, status and storage and false of the one thing the feature exists to do. applyVocabularyText had no caller anywhere outside its own tests, so an uploaded file changed a validation status line and not one rendered word. Twelve assertions covered the function; none covered the wiring, which is why a green suite never noticed. It is now consumed through app/renderer/src/text-boundary.ts, which App.tsx hands the storage handle on mount, and tests/ui/text-boundary.test.tsx asserts a replacement actually reaches rendered text. Replacement runs after translation so a personal rename is the last word. app/renderer/src/personal-vocabulary.ts is imported and fully wired into App.tsx: file load (loadVocabularyFile), clear (clearVocabulary), status (vocabularyStatus) and storage. Corrected 2026-08-23: the durability gap noted then is fixed. The renderer no longer reaches window.localStorage (in-memory only for a file:// origin) for this cache; it now goes through app/renderer/src/durable-storage.ts, which write-through-caches against the main process's control-plane settings.snapshot/settings.write/settings.remove actions (control-plane/settings-store.ts), persisted atomically (control-plane/atomic-file.ts) to settings.json under app.getPath('userData') the way the server inventory already is. Proved by a real relaunch on a headless desktop: set a value, force-killed then gracefully closed the app, inspected settings.json on disk between runs, relaunched, and confirmed the restored value without any manual reload.

per-element-toy-locks.note: The compiled console implements a real per-element lock/unlock mechanism (state.locks keyed by element id, tryUnlock() checking PIN or password, generated/console.tsx near line 3963) that is wired and functional. Missing against the contract: no OTP/TOTP option, no per-element lock-creation wizard reachable from a documented context-menu command, and no OS credential-vault storage - credentials live in plain component state.

support-tickets.note: Implemented 2026-08-23 as app/renderer/src/support-tickets.ts with four controls in the design, filed through App.tsx. The joke desk is played straight -- category, severity nobody honours, a locally generated ticket number, a status that advances and stops at Resolved, a canned reply -- and the resolution opens the application-data folder so the person can delete it themselves. It never deletes anything: `action` is the literal "open-folder" rather than a boolean, because a field that could say delete-folder is one somebody eventually sets to it, and an in-app deletion would owe the two-key confirmation gate. One line is never styled by the funny level and states that nothing is sent anywhere, no data is collected and nobody is reading it, because a user waiting for a reply that was never coming is the only genuinely harmful outcome here. A scan refuses any copy naming a real desk or implying a response time. The consequence line restates that the reset clears every toy lock and that a toy lock was never security.

unlock-ladder.note: app/renderer/src/unlock-ladder.ts is now imported and wired into the real per-element unlock dialog (App.tsx authVals/tryUnlock/finishLadderGrade): after three consecutive wrong PIN/password/TOTP attempts on a lock, tryUnlock calls ladder.issue() and, for a real dish or sums challenge, reuses the dialog's existing numeric keypad/dots and its mono-font method line (no new markup added, since the compiled design has no bound slot for a dish grid or sums list) to collect and grade a real answer through ladder.grade(). Confirmed reachable in the built app: right-clicking a screen opens 'Lock this element...', which opens the real wizard. A cleared challenge only closes the ladder UI and says the wait is over -- it never touches state.locks or the unlock dialog's own PIN/password/TOTP buffers, so the real credential is still required afterward (rule 1). The module's own 3-per-hour skip budget, single-use graded nonces, and never-refunding-the-attempt-budget rules are enforced by the module itself, unmodified. Two real gaps remain, both because editing the compiled design/generated output was out of scope here: the 'moles' rung has no visual board to render in this build, so it is treated as unreachable and the ladder falls back to 'wait it out' rather than faking a graded round; and because this app's per-element lock has no server-enforced or time-based lockout of its own (unlike the PIN/password it sits beside), 'clearing the wait' here dismisses the ladder UI but does not bypass any actual timed lockout, since none exists to bypass.

built-in-authenticator.note: app/renderer/src/totp.ts is now imported and wired into the real per-element lock (App.tsx pairAuth/lockNext/tryUnlock/authVals). pairAuth generates a real random secret with the Web Crypto RNG, computes the real otpauth:// pairing URI (pairingUri), and reveals both as copyable text through the app's real info panel -- never a remote QR service, and never any network call. lockNext refuses to finish a TOTP-including lock until pairAuth has actually run, and stores the real secret (not a placeholder) in the lock record. tryUnlock verifies a real RFC 6238 code via verifyCode (one step of skew) using the app's own numeric keypad, reusing it for a second 'totp' entry phase after any PIN phase completes. Confirmed reachable in the built app via headless CDP: registered a real TOTP secret through the real UI, independently computed the current code from that exact captured secret with totp.ts's own generateCode, typed the six digits back into the running app's real unlock dialog, and the app's own verifyCode accepted it and cleared the lock -- an earlier, stale code was correctly rejected first. Two real gaps remain, both because editing the compiled design/generated output was out of scope here: the QR box next to 'Pair the built-in authenticator' is a static decorative gradient with no bound slot for pixel data (not S(v...) anywhere in it), so the secret is shown as copyable text instead of a scannable image; and there is no confirmation-code re-entry step before the secret is treated as paired, because the 'Password+TOTP' method's wizard panel has no digit-entry control of its own to collect one (the PIN keypad belongs to a different method combination and would corrupt the user's real PIN if reused for this). The secret itself is stored in the same non-durable, non-OS-credential-vault state.locks the PIN and password already were before this change -- a pre-existing gap, not a new one, and still recorded as such.

attention-modes.note: Implemented 2026-08-23 as app/renderer/src/attention-modes.ts with five controls (att_focus, att_low, att_time, att_one, att_momentum) in the design, acted on through one prefix handler in App.tsx's setVal interception. Every mode is off by default and independently toggleable, which is the whole design: bundling them behind one switch means somebody who wants a quieter interface but not time nudges turns the entire feature off to escape the one part that does not suit them. Focus dims and never hides. Low stimulation composes with prefers-reduced-motion rather than overriding it, so a platform preference alone still reduces motion. Momentum respects a declined prompt for half an hour. Nothing is medical, scored or judgemental, and that is enforced by a scan over every string in the feature rather than left to review.

browser-extension-download-surfaces.note: This is a desktop console for an Asterisk PBX; there is no browser extension in this repository and no Start-download/Downloading/complete dialog surfaces.

offline-documentation-browser.note: app/renderer/src/docs-browser.ts implements article lookup/search over the bundled docs, app/renderer/src/generated/docs-bundle.ts (83 articles) is real bundled content, and app/renderer/src/docs-markdown.ts parses each article's body into headings/paragraphs/code/list blocks with resolved inter-article links. The `docs` destination is now a real screen on the App rail (compiled from design/Asterisk Console M3.dc.html, kind:'docs') wired in App.tsx (docsVals) with a real search field, a regex-builder toggle and palette, an article list, a rendered body pane and in-app link navigation. Headlessly driven in the built app (Electron via CDP): the article list shows all 83 titles/excerpts, selecting an article renders its real headings/paragraphs (no raw '#'/'[]' Markdown syntax), an inline `[text](href)` link inside one article's body navigated to the linked article, and a query with no matches shows an honest '0 matches' state. Remaining gap: no promoted screenshot/interaction evidence has been filed under this project's design-parity capture pipeline, so this stays 'partial' rather than 'verified'.

app-display-name.note: Implemented 2026-08-23 as app/renderer/src/display-name.ts: validation, persistence, one-action reset, and a per-surface split so the chosen name reaches the title bar, About and notifications while diagnostics, crash logs, issue reports, the update feed and the installer keep the shipped name -- a reader of a bug report has to know what software it came from. The whole safety of the feature is that IDENTITY is a frozen constant with no path from the display name: a rename that moved the application-data directory would orphan every stored profile, credential and history while the app looked freshly installed. Asserted directly, and proven by breaking it. Controls id_name and id_name_reset went into the design and came back through the compiler; App.tsx acts on them in the same setVal interception the language mode uses, and the display name is seeded back onto its field on mount.

guided-forms.note: app/renderer/src/endpoint-create.ts (WIZARD_CONTROLS, buildEndpointDraft) is imported and wired into App.tsx (line 14, 482, 488) to drive the endpoint-creation wizard with real validated fields and a generated secret. This is a genuine guided form for one flow (new PJSIP endpoint), not a system-wide guided-forms contract.
